papers.title: What Australian Health Practitioner Tribunals Decide, and What Automated Analysis Misses: 3,586 Decisions, 1999 to February 2026
papers.summary:
-  We classified 177 files: 80 data, 59 code, 13 documentation, 22 materials, 3 unknown.
-  We found 52 tabular data files and extracted 366 columns from 46 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  6 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (system_prompt.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; table36_human_reference_by_period.csv: 86% of columns are free text, not variables; table37_validation_summary.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; table38_coded_sample_estimates.csv: 75% of columns are free text, not variables; llm_test2_performance.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; test2_performance.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: system_prompt.txt, table36_human_reference_by_period.csv, table37_validation_summary.csv, table38_coded_sample_estimates.csv, llm_test2_performance.csv, test2_performance.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 366 columns; 8 columns have at least one potential issue (7 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 1 column with numeric values stored as text).

papers.title: Aging, Structural, and Neighborhood-Environmental Correlates of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Factor Burden Across U.S. Census Tracts
papers.summary:
-  We classified 86 files: 82 data, 2 code, 2 documentation.
-  We found 82 tabular data files and extracted 571 columns from 80 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (06_6f_wx_fit_summary.csv: 75% of columns are free text, not variables; Table1_sample_characteristics.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: 06_6f_wx_fit_summary.csv, Table1_sample_characteristics.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 571 columns; 2 columns have at least one potential issue (1 column of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic column for Age.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 333 files: 308 data, 13 code, 9 documentation, 2 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 1 tabular data file and extracted 119 columns from 1 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 119 columns; 34 columns have at least one potential issue (28 columns with numeric values stored as text; 9 columns whose name suggests personal information; 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column whose values look like personal information). 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Seven replicated genomic associations of myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME/CFS): a biobank study
papers.summary:
-  We classified 293 files: 32 data, 95 code, 57 documentation, 46 materials, 63 unknown.
-  We found 31 tabular data files and extracted 1462 columns from 31 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 3 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 1462 columns; 277 columns have at least one potential issue (262 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 13 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 1 column with numeric values stored as text; 1 column with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic column for Gender.

papers.title: Most coronial recommendations in Australia have no published response: a national analysis of findings and agency responses
papers.summary:
-  We classified 310 files: 122 data, 94 code, 28 documentation, 58 materials, 8 unknown.
-  We found 110 tabular data files and extracted 858 columns from 106 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  4 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (outputs/vic_case_review_2026-10/CASE_REVIEW.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; outputs_v2/tables/supplementary_stats_summary.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0.zip/Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0/outputs/vic_case_review_2026-10/CASE_REVIEW.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0.zip/Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0/outputs_v2/tables/supplementary_stats_summary.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: outputs/vic_case_review_2026-10/CASE_REVIEW.xlsx, outputs_v2/tables/supplementary_stats_summary.csv, Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0.zip/Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0/outputs/vic_case_review_2026-10/CASE_REVIEW.xlsx, Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0.zip/Coronial-NLP-Analysis-v2.1.0/outputs_v2/tables/supplementary_stats_summary.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 858 columns; 64 columns have at least one potential issue (50 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 8 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 6 columns of free text that may contain personal detail). 6 of 6 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
papers.summary:
-  We classified 67 files: 2 data, 50 code, 9 documentation, 4 materials, 2 unknown.
-  We found 2 tabular data files and extracted 25 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 25 columns; 25 columns have at least one potential issue (25 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 6 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race.
